extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Indian agents, Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Department of the Interior, and policymakers overseeing Indian agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, recommendations, and operational criteria for managing a U.S. Indian agency (1880-era): supply distribution, policing, schools, sanitation, land and resource protection, apprenticeships, and recordkeeping. Focused on practical administration and improvements proposed by agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize distribution of government stock and farming implements to actual farmers
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-issued stock and farming implements should be judiciously distributed, those Indians who were actual farmers and who had taken up and cultivated claims being first provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of implements issued in spring 1880 (oxen, heifers, bulls, wagons, plows, shovels, scythes, hay forks, etc.) and note that with an increased supply of oxen considerably more land could be cultivated; current number on hand (40 oxen) considered inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue passes only with official stamp/seal to prevent forgery
rubrics_metrics.description: No pass should be recognized as valid unless the official stamp or seal of the agent issuing it is attached; many forged passes circulate in the agent's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because not everyone is familiar with the agent's handwriting, an official seal or stamp is recommended to prevent unauthorized absences and forged passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide triplicate bill of lading and adequate shipping documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A triplicate bill of lading should be furnished the agent with every shipment to avoid confusion and long detentions of supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplies are often shipped in installments months apart; goods left in depots because navigation/rail closed cause shortages. Proper documentation and copies mitigate loss and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect and supervise forwarding of supplies to prevent neglect and unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department should direct inspectors or appoint competent agents whose specific duties shall be to see that all supplies are forwarded to their destination without detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect in forwarding supplies has caused uneasiness among agents and disturbances (e.g., the Ute outbreak). Regular oversight would reduce delays and related unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depose chiefs hostile to the government to facilitate settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Chiefs who are in the least hostile to the government should be strongly recommended for deposition because they obstruct Indians settling on separate farms and the equitable distribution of annuity goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too many chiefs retain influence by opposing individual claims and encouraging traditional dances; removing such chiefs will accelerate 'civilization' and reduce insubordination or war-like talk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent and remove white settlers ('squaw men') living on Indian land
rubrics_metrics.description: The migration and settlement of white men who live with Indian women and assert Indian rights on reservations is an 'infinite evil' that must be promptly stopped to prevent absorption of reservation lands and exploitation of Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These settlers often claim treaty rights, trade illegally, cheat Indians, and in some cases establish farms and cut hay/wood on the executive addition; urgent action is recommended to prevent permanent occupation of reservation additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and conserve timber resources around agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop wholesale destruction and drafts on timber (by military, squatters, and settlers) or the agency may have to be moved or supplied with fuel at large expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites consumption by garrison at Fort Yates and squatters; estimated cords required annually and rapid depletion within a few years unless checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate shop space and apprenticeships for trades training
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprentices (carpenter, blacksmith, shoemaking, tailoring, etc.) should be employed and given thorough instruction, which requires sufficiently large and equipped shops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seven apprentices employed (four carpentry, three blacksmith) are doing well but limited shop space prevents thorough instruction; recommends expanding shops and creating new trades (e.g., harness shop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient school and industrial buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Buildings are inadequate and a great drawback; larger school-buildings and an industrial boarding-school for both sexes (accommodating at least 50 pupils) are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If larger buildings provided, over 200 children could be instructed; also recommends new agent residence, warehouse for implements, elevator for grain, new flour-mill, root/vegetable house, and other infrastructure improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue passes sparingly and restrict during the working season
rubrics_metrics.description: Passes should be granted sparingly and only to deserving Indians (visiting sick relations, seeking work-related horses); refused when agent believes inciting speeches or hostile demonstrations would occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During May–October very few passes issued; indiscriminate visits during working season cause absenteeism, neglect of stock and crops, and reciprocal gift burdens on hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit inter-agency visiting to avoid distraction and resource drain
rubrics_metrics.description: Indiscriminate visiting of Indians from one agency to another is a great source of annoyance during the working season and should be curtailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visitors divert hosts from work, put a strain on hospitality (horses, blankets, clothing given), and create reciprocal obligations that leave hosts impoverished or 'in a state of nudity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate industrial boarding schools to teach trades, agriculture, and domestic skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial boarding-schools at a distance from homes are the chief means of educating Indians in practical trades, frugality, and industry; both sexes should attend schools combining academic instruction with practical labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: girls' farm school where girls milk, make butter, bake, knit, garden and attend English lessons; boys' school with six hours instruction plus chores, gardens, and individual patches of ground whose produce belongs to the boy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach English only in government schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching in the Indian language is condemned; day- and boarding-schools should be conducted in English only by competent white teachers to effect assimilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching in Indian language considered time and money thrown away; English-only instruction will better prepare students for industrial schools and assimilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use day schools as feeders and selection mechanism for industrial schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Day schools develop children sufficiently to enable teachers to select the most apt, brightest, and best for placement in distant industrial schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily attendance is small and irregular; despite parents' idleness, marked differences are observed in children attending day-schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and remunerate Indian police from tribes of good character
rubrics_metrics.description: Select police from different tribes, choosing only those with previous good behavior and moral character; organize night patrols and varied duties (watching camps, stragglers, squaw men), and pay them reasonably (comparable to War Department scouts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty men employed; night patrols restored order and prevented disturbances with soldiers. Remuneration currently inadequate given family responsibilities; recommends reasonable reward to maintain efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish hospital facilities and improve sanitary provision
rubrics_metrics.description: A regularly established hospital at the agency is necessary; it would be appreciated by Indians and be of incalculable benefit. Sisters of an order could supervise, and older girls could be trained as nurses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanitary conditions generally good but sporadic whooping-cough and pneumonia occurred. Hospital would centralize care for cases currently neglected and reduce mortality from consumption and scrofula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage excessive traditional dancing and tepee living for health reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive Indian dancing has caused many unnecessary ills (incipient consumption, lung disease); living in tepees is detrimental to health in severe winters; encourage log houses instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To promote health and 'civilization' government should seek to abolish dances and encourage comfortable log houses with doors and windows; many Indians are already adopting these practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage individual claims, fencing, and cultivation of land
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote settlement on separate farms and the fencing of individual claims; government should support reclamation and fencing (barbed-wire with cedar posts) to increase cultivated acres and yields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided of reclaimed and fenced agency farm, acreage planted (wheat, oats, corn), yields and estimated profit; also note communal planting of three large fields by 180 Indians and common hay-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide agricultural instruction and extension by trained pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail trained boys (or apprentices) to instruct Indians farming claims in proper plowing, planting, and operation of mowing-machines and scythes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In spring 1880, eight boys were detailed at Indians' request to teach proper farming methods and equipment handling; recommendation to continue such peer instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop agency industrial enterprises (mills, shops) under competent supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and improve agency mills, sawmills, tin-shop, carpenter and blacksmith shops under competent master mechanics to serve Indians and employ Indian workmen; expand capacity as demand increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current mills and machinery in some cases old/insufficient; improvements recommended (new flour-mill, elevator, harness shop) to increase output and training opportunities; largely Indian workforce with few white supervisors.
